fact: In patients with type 2 diabetes, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of dialysis, transplantation, or death due to kidney disease by 33% (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.52-0.86, p=0.0019).

fact: In patients with type 2 diabetes, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of end-stage kidney disease by 35% (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.53-0.81, p<0.0001).

fact: In patients with type 2 diabetes, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of acute kidney injury by 25% (RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.66-0.85, p<0.0001).

quote: SGLT2 inhibitors also reduced end-stage kidney disease (0·65, 0·53-0·81, p<0·0001), and acute kidney injury (0·75, 0·66-0·85, p<0·0001)

fact: In patients with type 2 diabetes and baseline eGFR 30-45 mL/min per 1.73 m², SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of dialysis, transplantation, or death due to kidney disease by 30% (RR 0.70, 95% CI 0.54-0.91, p=0.0080).

quote: there was clear, separate evidence of benefit for all eGFR subgroups, including for participants with a baseline eGFR 30-45 mL/min per 1·73 m2 (RR 0·70, 95% CI 0·54-0·91, p=0·0080)
